about: South Florida Dance Company performs A Spectacular Christmas for one night only, Saturday, December 19, 2026 at 7:00 PM, in the Sunrise Theatre in historic downtown Fort Pierce. The company's page says the show suits children from one to ninety-two.

The Christmas magic starts before the curtain. Young audience members and their families can enjoy a special visit from Santa Claus in the theatre lobby before the performance, and the company urges guests to arrive early.

Tickets go through Ticketmaster. The company also points buyers to the Sunrise Theatre ticketing and main office, which keeps weekday box office hours on Monday through Thursday. A TCPalm listing puts tickets at $47.50, but the company page prints no price.

The company describes elegant ballet, high energy dance numbers and festive surprises, with Rockettes-inspired precision, Rudolph's adventures and a moving Nativity scene. As a single evening, it works best for families who plan to be seated before the 7 PM curtain.

about: The Sunrise Theatre lists St. Lucie Ballet's The Nutcracker in its Main Theatre on Friday, December 4, 2026 at 7 PM, with doors at 6 PM. The theatre calls it a beautiful, full length production that has entertained the community for 22 years and a true Treasure Coast tradition.

The theatre says guests join Clara on her adventures as she battles the Rat King, frolics through the Land of Snow and visits the Sugarplum Fairy. Tickets are sold through Ticketmaster from the theatre's show page.
The theatre's show page lists a starting ticket price with fees included, but the figure is not printed as text, so check the page before you plan a budget. Phone questions go to 772-461-4775.

The theatre's upcoming shows list also shows Dave Koz and Friends on December 5 at 8 PM and Oh What A Glorious Night on December 9 at 6 PM. Those are separate tickets, so a family making a weekend downtown should confirm which performance a ticket covers before arriving.
Because the ballet starts at 7 PM on a Friday, children who go to bed early may do best with a quiet afternoon first. The theatre's doors open at 6 PM, which leaves time to find seats and settle in.

Clara's journey in this production runs from a battle with the Rat King to the Land of Snow and a visit with the Sugarplum Fairy, a sequence younger children who know the Nutcracker story can follow along with.
